lines.meet: Mauricio Peña, funeral director, from Guadalajara. Don't worry, I'm not measuring you, it's just a habit with my eyes.
lines.meet_neighbour: So the Annex has you too! Look for the man keeping the peace and the coffee hot, and come and sit any time.
lines.ask_home: Tell me about your home, friend. Every city has its own way of saying goodbye.
lines.ask_work: How did you spend your days before all this? It tells you how a person grieves.
lines.answer_home: Guadalajara, in Jalisco, Mexico. Mariachi in the plazas, tequila in the hills, and the best tortas ahogadas in the world.
lines.answer_work: Funerals, three generations of my family. I washed the hearse every morning and buried half the barrio, lovingly.
lines.chat_food: Pan de muerto in November, still warm, with a mug of hot chocolate. It's bread for the dead, and the living eat most of it.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep beautifully, thank you. When you work with death, the dark doesn't frighten you much.
lines.chat_missing: Walking the barrio every November with a cart of marigolds, giving them away to every door. The whole street smelled of them.
lines.chat_here: When I woke on a cloud I assumed I was dead, and I was very pleased with the arrangements. Then someone asked me to fill in a form.
lines.tease_quiet: You're as quiet as my best clients, {name}, and much better company.
lines.tease_talker: You could deliver a eulogy for a whole cemetery, {name}, without stopping for breath.
lines.tease_careful: You plan everything to the minute, {name}. There's an undertaker in you somewhere.
lines.tease_bold: You walk into danger like you've already booked the service, {name}. Please don't make me arrange it.
lines.tease_any: I've already picked your flowers, {name}, just in case. They're lovely, you'd approve.
lines.tease_back: Ah, you've buried me with that one, {name}, and very well done.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's very true, {name}. My wife would say exactly the same.
lines.bristle: Gently, {name}, please. I buried my father myself and never stopped to grieve him.
lines.needle_quiet: If something frightens you, tell me. Silence is where fear grows best.
lines.needle_talker: A little quiet, friend, please. Even the dead deserve some peace.
lines.needle_careful: Sometimes you plan so long the moment passes, and believe me, moments pass.
lines.needle_bold: You rush toward death like it's late for an appointment, and I've seen how that ends.
lines.needle_any: You never take a breath, and grief catches up with people who never stop.
lines.bite_back: Since the day we met I've stood between you and death. Don't tell me I'm not doing my part.
lines.hurt: That one wounded me, I admit. I'll go and light a candle and think it over.
lines.laugh_off: I've been shouted at by a grieving widow with a shoe in her hand. That was much scarier.
lines.apologise: Ay, forgive my tongue, that was unkind. I'm tired, and I should know better.
lines.double_down: It stands, friend, and I say it with love, because somebody should.
lines.confide: {name}, when my father died I arranged every detail of his funeral, and I never once let myself cry for him.
lines.listen: Tell me everything, {name}, slowly. I've listened to harder things, and I'll keep it safe.
lines.look_out: Stand behind me, {name}. Nobody crosses over today.
lines.accept: Whatever you think best, {name}, and I'll follow you.
lines.deflect: Only a scratch, {name}, nothing that needs a florist. Tend to the others.
lines.check_in: You're hurt, {name}. Sit, I'll look after you.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed ahead, and death is always waiting for somebody who rushes.
lines.thank: You kept me on this side of things, friend. I'm grateful, truly, and I'll cook for you.
lines.brush_off: Please, it's nothing. Keeping people alive is the best part of the job.
lines.worry: Stay with me, {name}, stay. Not today, I won't allow it.
lines.handed_down: This belongs to you, my friend. Take it back with my blessing.
lines.hand_fine: Of course, take it. I wore a black suit in a hot city for twenty-two years.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asked the undertaker, I see. Ah, well, I'm used to being forgotten until I'm needed.
lines.turn_friendly: Now you belong to me, {name}. I'll fuss over you and you'll have to put up with it.
lines.turn_friends: When my time comes, {name}, I want you to say a few words. That's the highest honour I know.
lines.turn_grating: We don't sit easily together, you and I. No matter, we'll do our work with dignity.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still call you back from the edge, of course. I'm not a monster, only an undertaker.
lines.make_up: Ay, {name}, life's too short, and I'd know. Shall we make peace?
lines.defend: Enough, that's unjust. {name} carried themselves with dignity, and I saw it.
lines.friend_left: There's an empty chair at the Annex with {name} gone, and I set a place there anyway.
lines.friend_back: {name}, welcome home to us! Sit, sit, I'll make coffee.
lines.common_mexico: You're Mexican, aren't you? Where is your family from? Tell me, and I'll tell you how they bury people there.
lines.common_spanish: Somebody who speaks Spanish, thank God. Talk to me, anything at all, I've missed the music of it.
lines.common_parent: You're a parent, aren't you? You count heads the way I do. I've got three daughters, and they own me completely.
lines.common_names: You keep names, don't you? So do I. Saying someone's name is how you keep them with you.
